title: An attempt stopped at its wall clock with nothing committed is collected as runner_error, not wall_clock_exceeded
body: subprocess classify (internal/exec/subprocess/collect.go) runs the no-commits check BEFORE the wall-marker check, and failureClass never consults the wall marker, so a worker stopped at its bound with zero commits persists failure_class=runner_error while the same worker with one commit persists wall_clock_exceeded. The run's feed says the bound fired, so the records disagree about one incident, and the class misdirects diagnosis exactly the way the quota-exhausted hint exists not to (SPEC §10.1). Found while writing pbb's acceptance test; left out of scope because the collect vocabulary is pinned in contracts/ and shared by three implementations, so the fix must go through a tick that owns that seam (likely also touching the herdr classify's no-commits path).
